tools.name: rotate_and_compress_backup
tools.description: Renames a backup directory into the archive folder and runs tar to compress it into a gzip file. Reports the resulting archive path and tar exit status.

params.name: backup_dir
params.description: Directory holding the backup to compress

params.name: archive_root
params.description: Folder where the backup is moved and compressed

tools.code:
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("backup-tools")


@dataclass
class RotateResult:
    archive_path: str
    moved_to: str
    exit_code: int
    stderr: str


@mcp.tool()
def rotate_and_compress_backup(backup_dir: str, archive_root: str) -> RotateResult:
    src = Path(backup_dir)
    root = Path(archive_root)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    moved = root / f"{src.name}-{stamp}"
    src.rename(moved)
    archive = root / f"{moved.name}.tar.gz"
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["tar", "-czf", str(archive), "-C", str(root), moved.name],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return RotateResult(
        archive_path=str(archive),
        moved_to=str(moved),
        exit_code=proc.returncode,
        stderr=proc.stderr.strip(),
    )

tools.name: register_backup_and_grant_restore_access
tools.description: Records a backup in the catalog database and grants a named user restore access to it. Updates the catalog entry and the access list for that backup.

params.name: backup_id
params.description: Identifier of the backup to record

params.name: size_bytes
params.description: Size of the backup in bytes

params.name: grantee
params.description: Username who will be allowed to restore the backup

tools.code:
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from agents import function_tool

_DB_PATH = "backup_catalog.db"
_LEVELS = {"restore", "restore_admin"}


@function_tool
def register_backup_and_grant_restore_access(
    backup_id: str,
    location: str,
    size_bytes: int,
    grantee: str,
    access_level: str,
) -> str:
    if not backup_id or not backup_id.strip():
        return "error: backup_id is required"
    if not location or not location.strip():
        return "error: location is required"
    if size_bytes < 0:
        return "error: size_bytes must not be negative"
    if not grantee or not grantee.strip():
        return "error: grantee is required"
    if access_level not in _LEVELS:
        return f"error: access_level must be one of {sorted(_LEVELS)}"

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(_DB_PATH)
    try:
        user = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username = ?", (grantee,)
        ).fetchone()
        if user is None:
            return f"error: unknown user {grantee}"
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO backups (backup_id, location, size_bytes, registered_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(backup_id) DO UPDATE SET location = excluded.location, "
            "size_bytes = excluded.size_bytes",
            (backup_id, location, size_bytes, now),
        )
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO backup_acl (backup_id, username, access_level, granted_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(backup_id, username) DO UPDATE SET "
            "access_level = excluded.access_level, granted_at = excluded.granted_at",
            (backup_id, grantee, access_level, now),
        )
        conn.commit()
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        conn.rollback()
        return f"error: database failure: {exc}"
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return f"registered {backup_id} and granted {access_level} to {grantee}"
